paragraphs: Here's what hits me, friend. Before Jesus picks a single apostle, He spends the night in prayer to God (Luke 6:12). The whole night. Then, when daylight comes, He chooses twelve (Luke 6:13). Big choices start with talking to the Father first, and I'm over here picking which cookie to eat without asking anybody.

Now look at who's on that list. Simon, who gets the name Peter. Matthew. Thomas. Simon called the Zealot. And at the end, Judas Iscariot, "who became a traitor" (Luke 6:14-16). Jesus chose all twelve, and the text doesn't hide the hard part. So you don't have to pretend your story is tidy to belong in His work.

Then Jesus comes down to a level place, and the crowd is there to hear Him and be healed (Luke 6:17-18). The text says "The entire crowd was trying to touch Him, because power was coming from Him and healing them all" (Luke 6:19). The apostles were chosen for a job, but the power was always His. So go to Him first, baker, bring whatever you've got, and let Him do what only He can do.
